title: Whole-House Vinyl Plank Installation in Everett: A Real Cost Example
meta: Whole-house vinyl plank in a 1,600 sq ft Everett home: $4,000 in Wills Flooring install labor plus $100 per stair, with material and prep quoted on site.

blocks.lead: For a typical 1,600 sq ft Everett two-story with 14 stairs, whole-house vinyl plank costs $5,400 in Wills Flooring installation labor: 1,600 × $2.50 for the floors plus 14 × $100 for the stairs.
blocks.detail: That is labor from our published price list. The plank itself, underlayment if the plank has none attached, tear-out of the old floors and any subfloor prep are quoted separately at the free in-home estimate, because they depend on what you pick and what we find.

blocks.html: The most common whole-house request we get in Everett comes from Silver Lake and Eastmont: a 1990s two-story with builder carpet upstairs, a vinyl kitchen, and a patchwork of laminate someone added in the living room. The owners want one floor, one color, top to bottom, and they want a number before they commit. So here is the number, built on a real floor plan, with every line that goes into it and the lines we cannot fill in until we have been in the house.

blocks.text: Why four lines wait for the estimate

items.title: The plank itself
items.text: Material is the biggest variable in a whole-house job, and it is your choice: core type, thickness, wear layer and look. We bring samples to the house so you can see them in your own light, then quote the exact quantity.

items.title: Old floor removal
items.text: Carpet comes up in minutes per room. Glued sheet vinyl and tile take hours. The example house has all three, which is why removal is quoted after we see it rather than guessed by the square foot.

items.title: Subfloor prep
items.text: Vinyl plank needs a flat subfloor, within about 3/16 in over 10 ft. Particleboard under old vinyl has to go. A 1990s Everett house is usually close, but we check with a straightedge before we quote.

items.title: Trim and transitions
items.text: Shoe molding or quarter round at the walls, transitions to any tile you keep, and stair nosings. Small line, but it is the difference between finished and almost finished.

items.html: Day 1: tear-out and prep downstairs. Laminate, vinyl and tile out, particleboard removed in the kitchen, subfloor checked and any high spots ground or low spots filled.
Day 2: main floor installed. Living, dining, kitchen, entry and hall in one continuous run, doorways undercut so the plank slides under the casings.
Day 3: upstairs. Carpet out in the morning, bedrooms and hall installed by evening. Bathrooms with toilets pulled and reset.
Day 4: stairs, trim and cleanup. Stair treads and nosings, shoe molding, transitions, appliances back in the laundry. Furniture can go back the same day; vinyl plank has no cure time.

blocks.text: When whole-house vinyl plank is the wrong move

a.title: It makes sense when
items: The house has a patchwork of carpet, laminate and vinyl
Kids, dogs or a rental mean water and scratches are normal
You want one floor with no transitions between rooms
The old floors have no hardwood hiding under them
Budget favors doing it once rather than room by room

b.title: Pause when
items: There is oak or fir under the carpet, common in Riverside and Bayside 1920s homes; refinishing is often cheaper and worth more
The subfloor is badly out of flat and leveling would cost more than the labor
You are in a Port Gardner condo with a sound rule that needs a specific underlayment
You only dislike one room; the 500 sq ft minimum still applies but a whole house is not required

blocks.title: One Everett-specific catch:
blocks.text: Many Silver Lake and Eastmont builder homes have particleboard underlayment under the kitchen and bathroom vinyl. Vinyl plank cannot float over it once it has swelled, and it should not be left under a floor you plan to keep for 20 years. We plan for its removal in the quote rather than discovering it on day one. If you are replacing carpet only, see what carpet-to-plank costs.
Make the estimate accurate before we arrive

items: Decide which rooms are in. A whole house usually means everything but closets under 10 sq ft; tell us if the bathrooms stay tile.
Count the stairs, including any landing. A landing is billed as floor area, treads at $100 each.
Lift a corner of carpet in a bedroom and a corner of vinyl in the kitchen. Photos of what is under each save a lot of guessing.
Note any soft or bouncy spots. They point to subfloor repair, which we would rather price up front.

Pick two or three looks before we come. Our mobile showroom brings full-size samples, and it is a 15-minute drive from the Lynnwood showroom to most of Everett. Details on what we install are on our vinyl plank page.

faq.q: How much does it cost to install vinyl plank in a whole house?
faq.a: Wills Flooring's installation labor is $2.50 per sq ft with a 500 sq ft minimum, plus $100 per stair. A 1,600 sq ft Everett home with 14 stairs is 1,600 × $2.50 + 14 × $100 = $5,400 in labor. Plank, underlayment, removal and subfloor prep are quoted at the free estimate.

faq.q: Is labor cheaper per square foot for a whole house than for one room?
faq.a: The published rate is the same $2.50 per sq ft either way, but a whole house uses the 500 sq ft minimum fully and needs fewer transitions, so the total per usable square foot is usually lower than doing three separate rooms in three separate years.

faq.q: How long does a whole-house vinyl plank installation take?
faq.a: About four working days for 1,600 sq ft with stairs, including tear-out. Larger homes, tile removal or subfloor leveling add a day. You can stay in the house; we usually finish one floor before opening the next.

faq.q: How much vinyl plank should I order for a 1,600 sq ft house?
faq.a: Plan on 8 to 10 percent extra for cuts and waste, so roughly 1,750 sq ft of plank. Diagonal layouts, herringbone and lots of small rooms push waste toward 12 to 15 percent. We calculate the exact box count at the estimate.

faq.q: Do you remove the old flooring and haul it away?
faq.a: Yes. Removal and disposal of carpet, laminate, vinyl, tile and particleboard are quoted at the estimate because they vary a lot by material. Carpet is fast; glued tile is slow. The quote lists each one so you can see what you are paying for.

faq.q: Can vinyl plank go over the old floors instead of removing them?
faq.a: Sometimes over a flat, well-bonded sheet vinyl or tile, never over carpet, laminate or swollen particleboard. Going over adds height at doors and stairs, so in a whole-house job we almost always recommend a clean subfloor.
